**Roster member identity and registration:** an accepted-deliberate member is identified by cargo-mutants' own mutation DESCRIPTION — the text after the coordinates on a tally line `{path}:{line}:{col}: {mutation}` — joined to `scripts/mutation-roster.toml` by its `member` key; never by `file:line:col` and never by function + column, both of which re-stale as code moves (a member's column can move while its description stays unique across the survivor set). The executable roster carries no line and no column, and two members may legitimately share one `(file, mutation)` pair (the two `replace == with != in stub_result` entries), which is why the comparison is a MULTISET. The roster is populated PER GATED UNIT, not for the whole citation home: it carries rows for the units a chunk has re-run — `conductor-cli` (`member-5`), `conductor-verify` (`member-4`) and `conductor-emit` (`member-emit-1`) — while `member-1`, `member-2` and `member-3` are citation-home numbering with no roster row, gaining one only when the epoch-boundary code audit re-runs the tier over their crate (a roster is a ledger of owed work, and only a re-run can shrink it). REGISTRATION is the `[[unit]]` declaration, never the row count: a `[[unit]]` table — optionally carrying a `files` list, workspace-root-relative, that scopes the tier to those paths via `-f` — registers a unit, so a registered unit whose survivors are all killed carries zero `[[entry]]` rows and PASSES when every graded tally agrees (empty `missed` and `timeout` multisets, each tally's count equal to `outcomes.json`'s, conservation holding); rows alone still register a unit; and because a scoped tier can generate nothing at all, a run producing 0 mutants is an explicit FAIL, never the clean sweep `cargo mutants` reports at exit 0.
